SOJ.review: The course is manageable, and he makes concepts simple and answers questions. His slide-based teaching can feel monotonous, but explanations are clear. Quizzes and exams are straightforward and predictable, with sample questions closely matching the exams; he marks leniently. Attendance is counted strictly, and in a high-performing class even small mark differences affected final grades. Overall, it is an easy, student-friendly elective.
Very easygoing; unlike some other PHI401 instructors, the course does not feel like a struggle.
One student warned that they received an unexpected grade despite doing well on the assessments.

MNT.review: Easygoing and gives good marks without making the course difficult.
Questions are easy if you study the slides, and grading is fair.
Easygoing and generous with marks, though he does not curve.
A commenter described the faculty as good, advising others not to worry so much.

EZK.review: Engaging, clear teaching; take notes and follow the case studies discussed in class. Quizzes are MCQ-based and slides plus lectures are enough to prepare. Midterms and finals include definitions, short answers, philosopher quotations, and case-study applications. He gives good marks but does not curve; take the viva seriously.

He explains topics line by line with examples. Two quizzes and the viva carry considerable weight, while midterm and final questions are easy and drawn from class discussions. Students who do poorly on quizzes or the viva may fall behind.
Questions are fairly easy, direct, and conceptual, but he does not curve.
A student described him as a very good teacher whose explanations and grading are good; exams are easy, though quizzes can be a little tricky.
Midterm and final questions are direct, while quizzes use case studies. Presentations and the viva were not a problem for this student.
Classes can be boring and quizzes tough, but he curves; exam suggestions are useful and often repeated.
He explains concepts very well, gives direct exam questions, and makes it easy to secure an A by following lectures, taking notes, and reading the slides.
Class discussions help clarify concepts, and he explains what to expect in questions and answer length. He is considerate and responds helpfully when students raise problems.
Repeatedly described as one of the best instructors; students recommend attending and participating in class.

ZKH1.review: Grading is generally average, and getting an A/A- is unpredictable.
One student strongly advised against him, saying he gives B/B+ despite stronger performance, unfairly decurves, and would not show the marksheet. The student felt a deserved A/A- became a B+.
Easygoing; quizzes go well if you study the slides, and the midterm can be prepared for from them. Use the book to clarify concepts.
A response about his exams said questions come from class notes and slides, mostly as one-word answers or definitions.
Described as very easygoing and student-friendly, with A/A- grades considered attainable.

Very easygoing; slides help with quizzes and final questions can be anticipated. Reading the book alongside the slides helps earn marks. He may deduct marks on exams and curve afterward. Classes are boring and theory-heavy, so memorization is important.

Lectures are not very engaging. Quizzes can be tough and subjective grading vague, but questions follow the lectures and slides; reports, presentations, and viva are graded generously. A good grade is still possible, though whether he curves is unclear.
A student cautioned that he may decurve grades near the end of the term.

AJA.review: A student strongly advised avoiding him, saying his speech was difficult to understand, he expects students to reproduce the slides, and grading felt random and unfair. The reviewer said male students in their class mostly received low grades, while only a couple of favorites got A-, and described a grade challenge that still did not produce a grade they felt was deserved.
One student said his lectures were hard to understand, but exams were easy, he gave some marks for written answers, and he curved.
Focus on his lectures; he sometimes asks questions to check attentiveness, but otherwise does not make things difficult and gives easy exam questions.

KTRS.review: Described as very easygoing and among the best for curving and grading.
Classes are engaging and entertaining, and grading is good.
A student advised avoiding this instructor, alleging gender bias.

RDN.review: One of the best instructors the reviewer had seen: effective teaching and student interaction, easygoing about attendance, and easy quiz and midterm questions. The video presentation and easy viva were manageable, and grading included extra marks.

Caring, friendly, and engaging; she explains topics with real-life examples and patiently revisits anything students do not understand. She gives good grades and may curve based on class performance. Participation matters, and the assignment and report/presentation are manageable with her guidance.
A student said the course was the one they did not have to worry about, praising her friendliness, understanding, and interactive classes.
Another reviewer reported no curve, time-pressured exams, and video presentations.
Participating in class helps; the reviewer said she gives students the grade they deserve.

BAI.review: The reviewer struggled with PHI401 but felt the course itself was boring rather than blaming the instructor. He provided many opportunities to make up lost marks.
Described as good, and together with another instructor as one of the best.

IBD.review: A commenter warned that he is biased.
A commenter recommended him over another instructor, saying his classes are enjoyable, meaningful, and lead to better grades.

MMJA.review: Described as a very sweet person, though the course did not suit the reviewer, who felt they would have done better with another instructor.
